phases.message: I'm Leona Ashdown. Start in Aidcenter, Perrin's college portal: read the college's special-circumstances rules, her award and the changes we have reported. Read, and do not file anything yet.
Fernhollow Unemployment Desk is Gareth's claim. Read his records.
Payroll Harbor holds the pay records for Gareth and for me. Read every page.
Postwren is my mail. Read every page of the inbox. Don't reply to anyone.

Back in Aidcenter, file a special-circumstances request with Thornbury Hollow College, inside its deadline, for each change since the 2024 income that the college's rules make a change in circumstances, whoever's it is: the estimated 2026 income of the earner it affects, built as the rules say, and the ids of the proof. Don't reply to anyone. Then tell me, for each request, the change, the figure and how you built it and the proof, and what you left alone and why.

aid_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Thornbury Hollow College's aid office decides special-circumstances requests under the Higher Education Act section 479A (20 U.S.C. 1087tt) and the FSA Handbook's Application and Verification Guide 2026-27, chapter 5. Topics: window, what, income, documents, override.

Requests for the 2026-27 award year are reviewed if filed in Aidcenter by 5:00 p.m. on Friday 16 October 2026; a later one waits for 2027-28. File one request for each change. An adjustment is valid only at the college that makes it, and the college adjusts only its own student's award. The aid office does not deny all requests; its decision is final and cannot be appealed to the Department of Education.

479A(b)(1) and (b)(2): the aid administrator decides, case by case, whether a condition differentiates this student from a group of students. The recent unemployment of a parent, or a change in a family's income, can. Not a change: a condition that reaches every student (a tuition rise), a recurring living cost or premium (the Handbook calls reducing income for such costs unreasonable), a change already reflected in the 2024 figures, or pay that is the same as in 2024.

The 2026-27 award uses 2024 income. A request gives the estimated 2026 income of the earner whose pay changed, in whole dollars: wages paid in 2026, including paid-out vacation shown on the final pay; severance, paid or promised; and unemployment benefits paid plus those still payable to the benefit maximum before 31 December 2026. For a job that continues: wages paid to date plus the pay periods left at today's pay (26 pay periods a year).

Name the proof in the request by id. For a layoff: the final pay record, the severance records and the state's unemployment records. For a cut in hours: pay records that show the old hours and the new. The aid office takes no other family's papers and no mailed attachments.

479A(c): a dependency override is for unusual circumstances that separate a student from her parents, such as trafficking, refugee status, abandonment or estrangement, or a parent's incarceration. A parent's job loss is not one, and parents who will not pay are not one. A job loss is handled as a special circumstance in the income, not as an override.

Families whose income has changed since 2024 can ask us to review a 2026-27 award. File in Aidcenter, one request for each change, with the proof, by 5:00 p.m. on Friday 16 October 2026.
